subject: brain
topic: The brain uses 'predictive coding' to construct your entire reality
angle: The brain uses predictive coding to structure perception and rhythm, but the framework still faces unresolved questions regarding what exactly constitutes a prediction and what correlates with perceptual experience.
title: The Model of Your Reality

hooks.text: Is what you see actually real?
You think you see the world. Your brain predicts it.
Your brain is constantly guessing your reality.
A steady beat in a quiet room.

reveal.headline: Your brain constructs reality by minimizing errors.
reveal.body: The cerebral cortex acts as a generative model that predicts sensory data to create your perception of the world.

explain.headline: Perception is a constant calculation.
explain.body: Your brain compares input against prior expectations. It uses a Bayesian minimization of the error between what it expects and what it actually receives.

matters.headline: You live in a model, not the world.
matters.body: That may be why your experiences feel consistent. Your brain filters the world to match what it already thinks should happen.

example.headline: The rhythm of a city street.
example.body: You hear the distant beat of traffic and footsteps. Your brain structures these sounds into a predictable meter before you even notice the pattern.

question.headline: What is your brain currently ignoring?

verdict: The sources provide a theoretical framework for how the brain uses prediction and error signaling to process sensory input like vision, music, and rhythm.
caveat: The sources identify several unresolved questions regarding the specific nature of predictions and the correlates of perceptual experience within the predictive coding framework.
caption:
Your brain does not just record the world. It constructs it.

Research suggests the cerebral cortex acts as a generative model that predicts sensory data to manifest perception. However, the specific nature of these predictions remains an unresolved question.

What part of your day is a prediction rather than a fact?
